title: Three-Week IB Spanish B Revision Plan
summary: IB Spanish B revision plan for November: triage weak topics, sharpen every language skill, practise timed papers, and protect essential rest time.
body_markdown:
Three weeks before a November exam session can feel both short and strangely long. There is enough time to improve, but not enough time to relearn two years of Spanish from the beginning. The answer is not to fill every available hour. It is to decide what deserves attention, practise it under increasingly realistic conditions, and leave enough energy to perform when the exam arrives.


This **IB Spanish B revision plan** follows a simple progression. Week one diagnoses and repairs. Week two combines skills under pressure. Week three rehearses, refines, and protects your focus. It works for SL and HL students, and it can be scaled down if Spanish is only one of several November subjects competing for your time.


### Your three-week plan at a glance


Week Main priority Spanish workload Desired outcome


Week one Diagnose and repair 45-60 minutes on 5 days Identify weaknesses and rebuild useful language


Week two Apply and integrate 60-75 minutes on 5 days Improve accuracy, speed, and task selection


Week three Rehearse and recover 45-90 minutes on selected days Complete timed practice without exhausting yourself


Each week should include writing, reading, listening, and active vocabulary recall. The current Language B assessment model gives external weight to all three assessed areas, while the course is organised around identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organisation, and sharing the planet. Revision should therefore cover both skills and themes rather than treating vocabulary lists as the entire course.


Before starting, open the[IB Spanish B resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-spanish-b) and gather your teacher feedback, marked work, vocabulary records, and the official materials supplied by your school. Keep one error log for the whole three weeks. A small record that you revisit is more valuable than a large folder you never open.


### Week one: diagnose before you revise


A common mistake is to begin with the topic you enjoy most. Familiar work feels productive because it moves quickly. Yet the purpose of week one is not comfort. It is information.
